provenance: Bernard Jacobson Gallery, London, whereby purchased by the previous owner. | Thence by descent to the present owner. |  | The work exemplifies Sol LeWitt's enduring commitment to exploring how simple geometric forms can generate complex visual and conceptual experiences. In this series, LeWitt treats the star not as a decorative emblem but as a structural device a shape whose symmetry and radiating logic can be systematically reconfigured. Each print in the set deploys bold, flat colour and crisply defined edges, allowing the viewer to focus on the underlying variations in form rather than on gesture or texture. The repetition across the six sheets creates a rhythm, a sense of unfolding possibilities within a constrained vocabulary, illustrating LeWitt's belief that art could emerge from rule-driven processes rather than expressive spontaneity. By reducing the star to a formal system, he transformed a familiar symbol into a platform for conceptual investigation, emphasising how small shifts in angle, colour, or arrangement could produce dramatically different visual outcomes.
